title: open-farm-link-panel
description: Home Assistant as an OFL Control Panel, and a strict mock Head Device to build it against

blocks.title: Lovelace card
blocks.details:
Source: `packages/ha-card/src/` (`ofl-garden-card.ts`, `styles.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `types.ts`)

- `ofl-garden-card` (Lit + TypeScript): the head unit plus one tray per Plant, and a per-plant view with moisture status, **Water now** and the light.
- Gets *structure* (plants, species, targets, entity ids) from the integration's `ofl/gardens` websocket command; live values come from `hass.states`; actions are plain entity service calls. The card never speaks OFL and never sees a credential.
- `npm run build:card` builds it into `custom_components/ofl/frontend/ofl-garden-card.js` (a committed artifact, so HACS users need no npm).
- Themed via HA CSS variables; strings in English and Russian.

children.title: Config flow
children.details:
Source: `custom_components/ofl/config_flow.py`

- Zeroconf discovery; `unique_id` = `garden_id`; rediscovery updates host/port of the existing entry.
- Pairing: button window, setup code (always runs the challenge first, so a wrong code is never sent), or an existing login.
- Creates a token named "Home Assistant", then lists all credentials on the device.
- Factory reset → pin mismatch → re-auth aborts with `device_reset`.
- **Bench mode** (`insecure: true`): for `open-farm-link-esp32` firmware without docs/22 support; behind an explicit confirm step.

children.title: OflClient
children.details:
Source: `custom_components/ofl/api.py`

- One client per device with its own aiohttp session, `TCPConnector(limit=1)`.
- Requests grouped in `async with client.batch()`; the session closes after each batch so the device's single connection slot is freed.
- **SPKI pinning** via `SpkiPin` (checked before any request is written); `expected=None` only during pairing.
- Retries span more than 5 s, past the device's idle timeout; after a request may have been sent only GET/PUT/DELETE are retried.
- Bench mode: plain `http://`, no pin, no `Authorization`.

children.title: Coordinator
children.details:
Sources: `custom_components/ofl/coordinator.py`, `custom_components/ofl/__init__.py`

- One config entry and one coordinator per Head Device (= one Garden).
- OFL has no push channel, so it polls: `6 + 3·plants` sequential requests per refresh, plus Hardware Calibration once per scope.
- Optional endpoints (Preferences, Grow Profile, Hardware Calibration) may 404; their entities are then not created.
- Without calibration, units come from the endpoint `format` (`raw_formats`).
- If the device clock source is `none`, it PUTs HA's time (option `sync_time`).

children.title: Entities
children.description: entity.py + sensor, switch, number, button, time, binary_sensor
children.details:
Sources: `custom_components/ofl/entity.py`, `sensor.py`, `binary_sensor.py`, `switch.py`, `number.py`, `button.py`, `time.py`

- Devices: the Garden (with System's shared modules) and one device per Plant, linked to the Garden.
- Vitals → sensors; binary Actuators → switches; other Actuators → numbers in physical units; Grow Profile `*_enabled` flags and vacation mode → switches; quiet hours → two time entities; `status` → problem binary sensors.
- **Water now** button: opens the valve and closes it from HA (the Actuators API has no duration).
- Entities come and go with hardware (`track_entities`). Unique IDs `{garden_id}_{scope}_{kind}_{key}` are used by the card: don't change them casually.

children.title: Card backend
children.details:
Sources: `custom_components/ofl/websocket.py`, `custom_components/ofl/frontend/`, `custom_components/ofl/diagnostics.py`

- `ofl/gardens` websocket command: each Garden's structure and the entity behind each value.
- Serves the built card at `/ofl_static/` and registers it on every dashboard (`add_extra_js_url`).
- Diagnostics never include the credential.

children.title: REST surface
children.details:
Sources: `packages/mock-server/src/index.ts`, `validate.ts`, `http.ts`, `scenarios.ts`

- The full OFL REST API; Plant and System share one sub-resource router.
- Every body validated (400 keeps only spec-defined fields); every error in the §16.2 JSON shape.
- Scenarios are reachable only through their own target's path; ids are device-assigned (`scn-N`); capability checks on create, update and Culture Pack import.
- Where the spec is silent, the chosen interpretations are listed in `AGENTS.md`.

children.title: Security and transport
children.details:
Sources: `packages/mock-server/src/security/identity.ts`, `security/device.ts`, `security/routes.ts`, `transport.ts`, `mdns.ts`

- ECDSA P-256 key and self-signed cert via `openssl`; `fingerprint` and `garden_id` derived per §22.2.
- Setup code, pairing window, tokens and PBKDF2 passwords, brute-force limit, factory reset.
- HTTPS, one connection at a time, 5 s idle timeout.
- mDNS: claims the first free `ofl-peer{N}.local`, TXT `pair=button` / `pair=code`.
- Key, setup code and credentials persist in `.data/<port>/`.

children.title: Simulated garden
children.details:
Sources: `packages/mock-server/src/state.ts`, `library.ts`, `derive.ts`, `engine.ts`, `history.ts`

- `library.ts`: hardware-model blueprints with their Hardware Calibration and default Settings.
- `derive.ts`: calibration on every Vitals/Actuators read and write, then Grow Profile sensor offsets.
- `engine.ts`: the Scenario engine plus a tiny physics (an open valve raises moisture, a running pump drains the tank).
- `history.ts`: 24 hourly records backfilled, then a sample every `OFL_HISTORY_PERIOD_S`.
- Garden data is in memory and re-seeds on restart.

children.title: Hardware control
children.details:
Sources: `packages/mock-server/src/control.ts`, `hardware.ts`

- A plain-HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:4380` standing in for the device's physical side; not part of OFL.
- Pairing button: `npm run button`, `npm run factory-reset`, `npm run mock:status`.
- `/hw/...`: plug or pull a Plant or module, set a sensor reading, fault a module, change the clock uplink. Capabilities are revalidated after each change.

The real rig (`open-farm-link-esp32` firmware, bench mode) is a separate repo; see `README.md`.

blocks.title: E2E tests
blocks.details:
Sources: `tests/test_e2e.py`, `tests/test_bench.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`

- Home Assistant's own test harness (`pytest-homeassistant-custom-component`, pins HA 2025.4.4) drives the integration.
- `test_e2e.py` runs against real mock-server processes in strict mode: pairing, entities, writes, websocket, factory reset, retries, zeroconf.
- `test_bench.py` runs against an in-process fake that answers like the ESP32 firmware (bench mode).
- Run: `npm run test:ha` (needs `.venv` and Node 20 via nvm).

blocks.title: Shared types
blocks.details:
Sources: `packages/shared/src/entities.ts`, `packages/shared/src/catalog.ts`

TypeScript types mirroring the OFL spec entities and the capability catalog, used by the mock. Maintained by hand against the spec in `specs/open-farm-link`.
